query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A High entropy alloy (HEA) with a modified surface, specifically a CrMnFeCoNi HEA with a nanocrystalline surface layer, can adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, resulting in enhanced wear resistance and surface protection.
generation.material_initial_state: Cu matrix in its pure form
generation.intervention: Depositing a 5 μm thick CrMnFeCoNi HEA layer with a nanocrystalline surface structure on the Cu matrix using magnetron sputtering at 300°C
generation.conditions: Vacuum environment, 10^-3 Pa pressure, and 100 W power
generation.structural_mediator: Interfacial diffusion and formation of a Cu-HEA intermetallic compound
generation.mechanism: The nanocrystalline surface layer of the HEA enhances interfacial adhesion with the Cu matrix through increased grain boundary area, leading to improved mechanical interlocking and diffusion bonding
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in adhesion strength compared to a bare Cu matrix, measured in MPa
generation.baseline: Pure Cu matrix without any surface modification
generation.boundary: Adhesion strength below 50 MPa indicates poor interfacial bonding
generation.uncertainty: The actual adhesion strength may vary depending on the specific HEA composition, surface roughness, and deposition conditions

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured adhesion strength is below 20 MPa, the hypothesis is falsified, indicating poor interfacial adhesion
